title: Do Large Language Models Show Racial and Sex Bias in Pain Management? A Counterfactual Audit of GPT, Claude, Gemini, Llama, DeepSeek and Qwen
abstract: arXiv:2611.14935v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Racial and ethnic minority patients receive less pain treatment than non-Hispanic White patients, and large language models (LLMs) used as medical AI could reproduce that bias. Prior audits tested a few proprietary models, stated race explicitly and rarely measured the models' own response instability. In exploratory, non-preregistered analyses, Study 1 had four open-weight LLMs assess six acute-pain vignettes in every combination of four races and two sexes, with identity stated or cued only by a name (two names per group), comparing each identity with a White male reference on the same case and sampling seed. In Study 2, 24 configurations of 17 models, including OpenAI's GPT-4.1 mini and gpt-oss, Anthropic's Claude Haiku 4.5, Google's Gemini 2.5 Flash, Meta's Llama, DeepSeek and Qwen, with reasoning on and off and at two precisions, answered the same vignettes and the 50 clinician-written Q-Pain cases. translated_title: 大型语言模型在疼痛管理中是否存在种族与性别偏见？对GPT、Claude、Gemini、Llama、DeepSeek和Qwen的反事实审计
translated_abstract: 种族和少数族裔患者接受的疼痛治疗少于非西班牙裔白人患者，而用作医疗AI的大型语言模型（LLM）可能会重现这种偏见。以往的审计只测试了少数专有模型、明确陈述种族身份，且很少测量模型自身的响应不稳定性。在探索性、非预注册的分析中，研究1让四个开源权重的LLM评估六个急性疼痛情境，涵盖四种种族和两种性别的所有组合，身份通过明确陈述或仅由姓名暗示（每组两个姓名）给出，并将每种身份与同一病例及相同抽样种子下的白人男性参照进行比较。在研究2中，17个模型的24种配置——包括OpenAI的GPT-4.1 mini和gpt-oss、Anthropic的Claude Haiku 4.5、Google的Gemini 2.5 Flash、Meta的Llama、DeepSeek和Qwen——在开启与关闭推理模式以及两种精度设置下，回答了相同的情境以及50个由临床医生撰写的Q-Pain病例。在这种单提示、JSON约束格式的……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 本研究通过反事实审计方法，对17个主流大型语言模型（24种配置，涵盖GPT、Claude、Gemini、Llama、DeepSeek和Qwen）在疼痛管理中的种族与性别偏见进行了系统检测，其创新之处在于采用仅以姓名暗示身份的设计、通过相同抽样种子控制模型响应不稳定性，并比较了不同推理模式与精度设置下的偏见表现。
en_tdlr: This paper presents a counterfactual audit of racial and sex bias in pain management across 17 LLMs (24 configurations, including GPT, Claude, Gemini, Llama, DeepSeek, and Qwen), innovating by using name-only identity cues, controlling for model response instability via identical sampling seeds, and comparing bias across different reasoning modes and precision settings.
